$comment: Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md. Standard 20 owns message wording for the whole framework: forms and error-presentation rules govern association and classification, and defer here for what the text says.

rules.title: Failure and consequence copy says what happened and what to do
rules.description: A message reporting a failure or a consequence names what happened and what the user can do about it, where the application holds that information.
rules.rationale: 'Something went wrong' spends the user's attention and returns nothing. Where the system knows more, withholding it converts a recoverable situation into a dead end.
rules.remediation: Say what failed and what action is available, and reserve generic wording for cases where the system genuinely knows nothing more.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether a message is actionable depends on what the system knew at that moment, which is not recoverable from the message's text.

rules.title: Action labels describe the action
rules.description: Where a more specific label reads naturally, an action is labeled with what it does rather than with a generic affirmative.
rules.rationale: A specific label lets the user confirm their intent against the button rather than against the sentence above it — which matters most in exactly the dialogs people stop reading.
rules.remediation: Replace a generic label with the action, where doing so does not produce unnatural wording.
rules.$assuranceNote: Standard 20 R3 is explicit that this is a preference with a purpose, not a prohibition on the word 'OK'. Detecting it mechanically would produce a rule the standard does not state.
